title: Distributed training overview
text: Data parallelism replicates the model on multiple GPUs while splitting batches. Expert parallelism shards MoE layers so each device holds a subset of experts. All-to-all communication dispatches tokens to the experts selected by the router.

title: Curriculum mixing note

title: Shard immutability

title: MoE load balancing
text: Router auxiliary losses encourage uniform expert utilization. Without load balancing, a few experts receive most tokens and others idle, wasting capacity and destabilizing gradients.

title: Run ledger semantics
text: Consumption ledgers record which shard windows were trained at each step. Crash recovery replays from the last committed checkpoint plus ledger cursor.

title: Ultra reasoning: invariant
text: Consider tokens routed to experts each step. Load balancing loss uses fraction of tokens per expert vs router probability mass. If router collapses to one expert, auxiliary loss spikes, gradient pushes probabilities toward uniform until utilization variance drops.

title: Long context: policy memo
text: Internal memo draft: The training data execution system must treat tokenizer identity as immutable for a run family. Shards reference tokenizer_hash in every manifest row. Admission gates reject documents missing cleaning lineage or with eval overlap flags. Curriculum YAML defines stage bands; the sampler reads registry entries marked opus_eligible. Anneal reserves high-quality indic text for late-stage loss weighting. Firewall checks run before batch tensors receive loss masks. Never-train rows remain in the registry for overlap detection but never enter consumption ledgers. Crash recovery depends on atomic shard writes and append-only ledgers keyed by run_id and step.
